newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end lower, finance stocks weaken.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end lower, finance stocks weaken.

text.p: Weakness in index-heavy finance stocks Maybank and AMMB Holdings and buyer apathy dragged down Kuala Lumpur blue chips on Tuesday, although small-capitalised shares advanced.
"The gains are mainly on the Second Board," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities. "Generally, it's very mixed."

The Composite Index of 100 key blue chips ended 6.84 points or 0.61 percent lower at 1,110.36, after achieving a high of 1,121.45. Maybank and AMMB together comprise about 10 percent of the index's weighting.
The Second Board index of smaller-capitalised shares added 2.26 points or 0.40 percent to 564.80.

Steve Lim, fund manager at HLG Asset Management, said: "Some mutual funds may be selling ahead of their book closures on June 30, but most of the funds who wanted to sell down Malaysian stocks probably have already done so."
As for his fund, he added: "We are buying, but we are trying to buy slowly." He said he was focusing on defensive stocks with good growth prospects.
Volume topped 219 million shares valued at 1.53 billion ringgit, with gainers taking a slim 275 lead over 268 losers.
